mika: quick ping — onboarding of vela_light -> gemma_bridge int8 showed a weird punctuation-stutter during summarization: sequences end up with repeated ellipses like 'This suggests... ... ...' around token 180-195. repro attached.

jun: that's odd. is the tokenizer normalization step enabled during conversion? soft-hyphen (U+00AD) folding can collapse tokens unexpectedly under some token merges. also could be per-layer requant rounding noise creating repeated punctuation when soft-stop triggers. did you run token roundtrip?

mika: minimal repro below:
```
# convert
python tools/convert_model.py --src vela_light --dst vela_gem_br --quant int8 --calib-samples 512 --preserve-vocab
# eval
python tests/summarize_smoke.py --model vela_gem_br --input tests/cases/punct-stutter.txt --max-tokens 300 --temperature 0.0
```
snippet: 'Conclusion: This suggests... ... ... The model recommends...' (repeat happens reproducibly)

priya: can you paste a token id slice around where it repeats? run --dump-tokens --context 256 and also run tokenizer fingerprint (hash first 2048 ids).

mika: token dump: ids 1789, 42, 11, 11, 11, 59, ... where 11 is '.' in this vocab. tokenizer fingerprint (first 2048) = 0x9a3fbe12

jun: triple dot compression collapsing into repeated '.' sounds like two possibilities: (A) tokenizer normalization mapped soft-hyphen or zero-width joiner into a token that later collapses into '.' due to merge rule change during vocab-preserve; (B) quantized logits post-softmax get flattened so beam/deterministic decoding picks same '.' token repeatedly because of a narrow but repeated peak. How does the non-quantized baseline behave?

mika: float32 baseline (pre-convert) produces single '...' as expected. candidate int8 shows the repeat. logits around token 182:
- float top logits: [6.1, 2.2, 1.0] ('.' is 6.1)
- int8 top logits: [6.05, 6.02, 5.9] ('.' is 6.05, next '.' picks again due to tiny rounding)

priya: those int8 logits look like quantization saturation making nearby tokens nearly equal, so greedy/deterministic decoding can oscillate. Two mitigation directions: 1) per-channel (per-out) quant scaling for last LM head to preserve relative margins, 2) run a tokenizer normalization pass to remove soft-hyphen variants before fingerprinting and CI, so we catch token merge differences early.

jun: agree. Also add a tiny sanity eval that runs deterministic decode on 10 canonical examples and compares token-level edit distance to baseline; fail if repeated punctuation > threshold. For conversion flags, propose --head-output-perchannel-scale and --normalize-unicode=NFKC (default off to preserve original).

mika: implemented a local patch to use per-channel output scales for the lm_head during calibration (multipliers computed from activation stats). re-ran smoke: punctuation stutter reduced but PPL on long summarize increased by +0.9. token-fingerprint changed (0x9a3fbe12 -> 0x9a40c1ff) because we normalized unicode.

priya: +0.9 PPL might be acceptable if user-visible behavior improves. let's quantify user impact: run our quality-eval set (5k summaries) and compute fraction with punctuation-stutter and delta ROUGE. If stutter goes from 1.2% -> 0.05% and ROUGE drop <0.5, we keep the per-channel lm_head scale. Also record a conversion note about normalized fingerprint change.

mika: running batch now on a dev node (ETA ~20m). Also created an onboarding lint that checks for soft-hyphen presence in vocab and prints a warning if tokens map to '.' when normalized.

ci-bot: nightly-onboard/vela_gem_br-int8 reported failure: summarizer-stutter-check failed (see https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/5019)

jun: thanks, looks consistent with local. once batch done, open PR with: (a) per-channel lm_head flag, (b) unicode-normalize option in conv-tool, (c) small deterministic decode gate. I'll review.

priya: one more ask — add a tiny calibration sanity plot to onboarding artifacts: lm_head scale histogram before/after so we can inspect outliers. that often reveals a single head saturating.

mika: done, attaching histograms in follow-up comment. will post summary numbers here when complete. :rocket:
